Match List I with List II

    List - II
  

  
    (A)
    Glucose/$\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}/\Delta$
    (I)
    Gluconic acid
  
  
    (B)
    $\text{Glucose}/\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$
    (II)
    No reaction
  
  
    (C)
    $\text{Glucose}/\mathrm{HI}/\Delta$
    (III)
    n-hexane
  
  
    (D)
    Glucose/Bromine water
    (IV)
    Saccharic acid
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Glucose has no free COOH group, so the weak base $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ does not react with it: A–II.

Nitric acid oxidises both the CHO group and the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ group of glucose to COOH, giving saccharic (glucaric) acid: B–IV.

Prolonged heating with HI reduces glucose to n-hexane, which shows that its six carbon atoms form a straight chain: C–III.

Bromine water is a mild oxidant that oxidises only the CHO group to COOH, giving gluconic acid: D–I.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement - I: Noble gases have very high boiling points.

Statement - II: Noble gases are monoatomic gases. They are held together by strong dispersion forces. Because of this they are liquefied at very low temperature. Hence, they have very high boiling points.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Option A is the correct answer. Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Noble gases actually have low boiling points, not high. This is because noble gases are indeed monoatomic gases that exist as single atoms. They have a completely filled valence shell and do not easily form chemical bonds with other atoms. As a result, the intermolecular forces present in noble gases are only temporary dipole-induced dipole attractions, also known as dispersion forces (or London forces). However, these dispersion forces are very weak compared to other types of intermolecular forces like hydrogen bonding or dipole-dipole interactions that occur in other substances.

The dispersion forces in noble gases are weak because these gases are non-polar and since they are monoatomic, the electron cloud around the atom is symmetrical, meaning that there are no permanent dipoles within the molecules. As the atomic size of noble gases increases down the group, the dispersion forces do increase in strength due to the larger electron cloud that can be more easily distorted, resulting in higher boiling points for the heavier noble gases. Still, compared to other substances, the overall strength of the dispersion forces in noble gases is low, which means they can be liquefied at low temperatures and hence their boiling points are low, not high.

Therefore, the correct statement would be: "Noble gases are monoatomic gases. They are held together by weak dispersion forces. Because of this they are liquefied at very low temperatures. Hence, they have very low boiling points."
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: A species having carbon with sextet of electrons and can act as electrophile is called
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The species described as having a carbon atom with a sextet of electrons—that is, six electrons in its valence shell—capable of acting as an electrophile (an electron-pair acceptor) is called a carbocation. Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option D
carbocation

[IMG]


Here's a brief explanation of each option:

Option A: Pentavalent carbon - This term is not commonly used in organic chemistry, and it refers incorrectly to a carbon with five bonds, which contradicts the tetravalency of carbon.

Option B: Carbon free radical - This species has a carbon atom with an unpaired electron (a septet, or seven valence electrons). It is highly reactive but is not typically classified as an electrophile because it seeks to pair its single unpaired electron rather than accepting a pair of electrons.

Option C: Carbanion - This anion has a carbon atom with three bonds and a pair of electrons, which in total gives eight valence electrons. It is nucleophilic (electron-pair donor) rather than electrophilic.

Option D: Carbocation - A carbocation is indeed a carbon species with only six valence electrons and thus has an empty p-orbital that can accept a pair of electrons, making it electrophilic. Carbocations are usually trigonal planar in structure and carry a positive charge.

text: Identify the mixture that shows positive deviations from Raoult's Law
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In pure acetone the molecules are held by dipole–dipole attractions. Non-polar $\mathrm{CS}{}_{2}$ molecules come between them, and the acetone–$\mathrm{CS}{}_{2}$ attractions are weaker than the acetone–acetone and $\mathrm{CS}{}_{2}$–$\mathrm{CS}{}_{2}$ attractions.

Molecules therefore escape more easily from the mixture, and its vapour pressure is higher than Raoult's law predicts: $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{CS}{}_{2}$ shows positive deviation ($\Delta _{mix}H>0$, $\Delta _{mix}V>0$).

In the other three mixtures hydrogen bonding between unlike molecules (N–H$\cdots$O=C in acetone–aniline, C–H$\cdots$O=C in chloroform–acetone, C–H$\cdots π$ in chloroform–benzene) makes A–B attractions stronger, so they show negative deviation.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The correct statements from following are:

A. The strength of anionic ligands can be explained by crystal field theory.

B. Valence bond theory does not give a quantitative interpretation of kinetic stability of coordination compounds.

C. The hybridization involved in formation of $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$ complex is $\mathrm{dsp}^{2}$.

D. The number of possible isomer(s) of cis- $[\mathrm{PtCl}_{2}(\mathrm{en})_{2}]^{2+}$ is one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A: crystal field theory treats ligands as point charges, so anionic ligands should split the d orbitals most; in fact anionic ligands such as $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ lie at the weak-field end of the spectrochemical series. CFT cannot explain the strength of anionic ligands, so A is false.

Statement B: valence bond theory gives no quantitative interpretation of the thermodynamic or kinetic stability of coordination compounds; this is one of its limitations, so B is true.

Statement C: in $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$, $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$. The strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ ligands pair the two unpaired 3d electrons, leaving one 3d orbital empty; this 3d, the 4s and two 4p orbitals form $dsp^{2}$ hybrids, giving a square planar, diamagnetic complex. C is true.


[IMG]

Statement D: $\text{cis-}[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}]{}^{2+}$ has no plane of symmetry, so it exists as two non-superimposable mirror images (d and l forms). It has two isomers, not one, so D is false.


[IMG]

The correct statements are B and C only.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:

Assertion A: Alcohols react both as nucleophiles and electrophiles.

Reason R: Alcohols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium and aluminum to yield corresponding alkoxides and liberate hydrogen.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Alcohols react as nucleophiles when the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond breaks and the oxygen lone pair attacks an electrophilic centre, as in esterification with a carboxylic acid or an acid chloride.

Alcohols react as electrophiles when the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond breaks: the protonated alcohol $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ is attacked at carbon by a nucleophile, as in $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{HBr}\longrightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. So Assertion A is true.

Alcohols react with active metals such as Na, K and Al to give alkoxides and hydrogen, for example $2~\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}+2\mathrm{Na}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{ONa}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$. So Reason R is true.

Reason R shows only the acidic character of alcohols (loss of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ from the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond); it says nothing about alcohols reacting as electrophiles, so it does not explain A.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: Identify the factor from the following that does not affect electrolytic conductance of a solution.
options: The nature of the electrolyte added.
The nature of the electrode used.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electrolytic conductance is due to the movement of ions through the solution, so it depends on the number of ions present and how fast they move.

The nature of the electrolyte (strong or weak, charge and size of its ions), the nature of the solvent (its polarity, which decides ion solvation, and its viscosity) and the concentration of the electrolyte all change the number or the speed of the ions, so each of them affects conductance.

The electrodes only carry current into and out of the solution; their material does not change the ions or their mobility in the solution, so the nature of the electrode does not affect electrolytic conductance.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
Integrated rate law equation for a first order gas phase reaction is given by (where $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}$ is initial pressure and $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}$ is total pressure at time $t$)
(Take the reaction to be of the type $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{llll} \mathrm{A}\to  & \mathrm{B} & + & \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}} & 0 &  & 0 \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{x} & \mathrm{x} &  & \mathrm{x} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{x} \\ \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}} \\ =2\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}} \\ \mathrm{K}=\dfrac{2.303}{t}\log \dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{2\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}} \end{array}$

Hence option A is correct. Option C has the same ratio but without the $\log$, so it is not the integrated rate law.

text:
Match List I with List II

  
    
    List - I (Technique)
    
    List - II (Application)
  

  
    (A)
    Distillation
    (I)
    Separation of glycerol from spent-lye
  
  
    (B)
    Fractional distillation
    (II)
    Aniline - Water mixture
  
  
    (C)
    Steam distillation
    (III)
    Separation of crude oil fractions
  
  
    (D)
    Distillation under reduced pressure
    (IV)
    Chloroform - Aniline
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To match List I (Technique) with List II (Application), we need to understand the relevance of each distillation technique:

1. Distillation is typically used for separating components of mixtures who have a significant difference in boiling points.

Application: Chloroform - Aniline.

2. Fractional distillation is used for separating mixtures of liquids with closer boiling points by using a fractionating column.

Application: Separation of crude oil fractions.

3. Steam distillation is generally used for compounds that decompose under high temperatures and are insoluble in water.

Application: Aniline - Water mixture.

4. Distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) is used for compounds with very high boiling points to avoid decomposition.

Application: Separation of glycerol from spent-lye.

Therefore, the correct match is:

Option D
 A-IV (Distillation - Chloroform - Aniline)
 B-III (Fractional distillation - Separation of crude oil fractions)
 C-II (Steam distillation - Aniline - Water mixture)
 D-I (Distillation under reduced pressure - Separation of glycerol from spent-lye)

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: IUPAC name of $\mathrm{HO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-(\mathrm{CH}_{2})_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$ is 7-hydroxyheptan-2-one.

Statement II: 2-oxoheptan-7-ol is the correct IUPAC name for above compound. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Written out, the compound is a seven-carbon chain ending in an acetyl group ($-\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$ is $-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{CH}_{3}$, a ketone, not a methoxy group):

$\mathrm{HO}-\mathrm{C}^{7}\mathrm{H}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{6}\mathrm{H}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{5}\mathrm{H}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{4}\mathrm{H}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{3}\mathrm{H}_{2}-\mathrm{C}^{2}\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}^{1}\mathrm{H}_{3}$

The ketone ranks above the alcohol, so it is the principal group (suffix "-one") and $-\mathrm{OH}$ is cited as the prefix "hydroxy".

Numbering from the $\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ end gives the carbonyl carbon the lowest locant, 2, and places $-\mathrm{OH}$ on C-7, so the name is 7-hydroxyheptan-2-one and Statement I is correct.

The name 2-oxoheptan-7-ol takes the lower-ranking $-\mathrm{OH}$ as the suffix and the ketone as the prefix "oxo", so Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: Consider the following reaction at $298\mathrm{K}$: $\frac{3}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2(g)}⇌\mathrm{O}_{3(g)};\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}=2.47\times 10^{-29}$. $\Delta _{r}G^{⊖}$ for the reaction is $_________$ $\mathrm{kJ}$. (Given $\mathrm{R}=8.314\mathrm{JK}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)

Hence, the answer is 1.

text: Number of alkanes obtained on electrolysis of a mixture of $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COONa}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electrolysis of aqueous sodium carboxylates (Kolbe electrolysis) gives alkyl radicals at the anode:

$\mathrm{RCOO}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{RCOO}{}^{\bullet ~}+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\mathrm{RCOO}{}^{\bullet ~}\longrightarrow \mathrm{R}{}^{\bullet ~}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$

The mixture therefore gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\bullet ~}$ from $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}$ and $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}{}^{\bullet ~}$ from $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COONa}$, and any two radicals can couple:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\bullet ~}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\bullet ~}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\text{(ethane)}$

$\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}{}^{\bullet ~}+\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}{}^{\bullet ~}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\text{(butane)}$

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\bullet ~}+\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}{}^{\bullet ~}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\text{(propane)}$

Three alkanes are obtained: ethane, propane and butane.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: The 'Spin only' Magnetic moment for $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{2+}$ is $_________$ $\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{BM}$. (given $=$ Atomic number of $\mathrm{Ni}:28$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ nickel is in the $+2$ state: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{8}$, and the complex is octahedral.

In an octahedral field eight d electrons are arranged as $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$ irrespective of the ligand field strength, because the $t_{2g}$ set can hold only six electrons. The two $e_{g}$ electrons remain unpaired, so $n=2$ (outer-orbital $sp^{3}d^{2}$ complex).


[IMG]

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{2\times 4}=\sqrt{8}=2.83\text{BM}=28.3\times 10^{-1}\text{BM}$

To the nearest integer, the value is 28.

Hence, the answer is 28.

text: One Faraday of electricity liberates $x\times 10^{-1}$ gram atom of copper from copper sulphate. $x$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the value of x when one Faraday of electricity liberates x times $10^{-1}$ gram atom of copper from copper sulphate, we need to understand how electricity interacts with copper ions in solution. The key reaction is:
$\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Cu}$
This shows that copper ions $(Cu^{2+})$ gain two electrons $(e^{-})$ to become copper metal (Cu). From electrochemistry, we know that:
2 Faradays of electricity are required to deposit 1 mole (or 1 gram atom) of copper.Therefore, 1 Faraday will deposit half of that amount, which is 0.5 mole, or in other terms, 0.5 gram atom of copper.Expressing 0.5 in the form of x times $10^{-1}$ gives us $5\times 10^{-1}$.This means x equals 5.

text:
Molar mass of the salt from $\mathrm{NaBr},\mathrm{NaNO}_{3},\mathrm{KI}$ and $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}$ which does not evolve coloured vapours on heating with concentrated $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is $________$ $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}{}^{-1}$.

(Molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}:\mathrm{Na}:23,\mathrm{N}:14,\mathrm{K}:39,\mathrm{O}:16,\mathrm{Br}:80,\mathrm{I}:127,\mathrm{F}:19,\mathrm{Ca}:40)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On heating with concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$, $\mathrm{NaBr}$ gives reddish-brown $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ vapours, $\mathrm{KI}$ gives violet $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ vapours and $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{3}$ gives $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$ vapours that decompose to brown $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{CaF}{}_{2}$ gives only colourless $\mathrm{HF}$, because $\mathrm{HF}$ is not oxidised by the acid:

$\mathrm{CaF}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{HF}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{CaF}{}_{2}=40+2\times 19=78\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Hence, the answer is 78.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
The number of species from the following in which the central atom uses $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybrid orbitals in its bonding is $__________$.

$\mathrm{NH}_{3},\mathrm{SO}_{2},\mathrm{SiO}_{2},\mathrm{BeCl}_{2},\mathrm{CO}_{2},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{CH}_{4},\mathrm{BF}_{3}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The hybridisation of the central atom follows from its steric number (σ bonds + lone pairs), or for a network solid from its coordination.

$\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ has 3 σ bonds and 1 lone pair, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ has 2 σ bonds and 2 lone pairs, and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$ has 4 σ bonds; each has steric number 4, so the central atom is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$.

$\mathrm{SiO}{}_{2}$ is a three-dimensional covalent network in which every Si atom is bonded to four O atoms at the corners of a tetrahedron (Si does not form $pπ$–$pπ$ double bonds), so Si is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$.

$\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$ (2 σ bonds + 1 lone pair) and $\mathrm{BF}{}_{3}$ (3 σ bonds) are $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$; $\mathrm{BeCl}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ (2 σ bonds, no lone pair) are $\mathrm{sp}$. $\mathrm{BeCl}{}_{2}$ is taken as the discrete linear molecule (Be is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ only in the chain polymer of the solid), whereas $\mathrm{SiO}{}_{2}$ has no stable molecular form and is taken as the network.

The $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ species are $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{SiO}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
